excerpt: Metorial gives developers official TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs to connect AI agents to tools in minutes.
Get up and running with Metorial in under 5 minutes
OAuth lets your users authorize access to their accounts on services like Slack, GitHub, Google Calendar, and more.
Beyond the pre-built integrations in the Metorial catalog, you can upload your own MCP server code and let Metorial host it.
You can attach multiple providers—from the same provider or different ones—in a single session. The tools from all of them are merged and exposed to your AI.
Tool filters let you control which tools from a provider are available during a session.
You can optionally pin a deployment to a specific version to prevent automatic updates—useful when you need stability across a production environment.
Portals are branded places where users discover and connect approved integrations, skills, and MCP access.
Teams review traces, sessions, tool calls, auth events, and failures after work runs.
Magic Skills package repeatable workflows so teams can publish and govern useful agent work.
Use a remote MCP server when the provider already offers an MCP endpoint. Metorial connects to it and you can use it like any other provider on Metorial.
RBAC, SAML SSO, and IAM built in so agent access follows your existing security model.

The Metorial SDK throws typed errors that help you identify and handle specific failure scenarios.
The Vercel AI SDK integration (`@metorial/ai-sdk`) is the recommended way to use Metorial in TypeScript applications.
Metorial supports all of these OpenAI-compatible providers.
The OpenAI provider integration lets you use Metorial's MCP tools with OpenAI's GPT models, including GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.
The Anthropic provider integration lets you use Metorial's MCP tools with Claude models (Sonnet, Opus, and Haiku).
The Google provider integration lets you use Metorial's MCP tools with Google's Gemini models.
Beyond the pre-built integrations in the Metorial catalog, you can upload your own MCP server code and let Metorial host it. Metorial handles scaling and monitoring.
You can generate both publishable and secret API keys in your Metorial dashboard by navigating to Developer → API Keys and clicking Create API Key.
Each environment has its own provider deployments, API keys, authentication configs, and logs, so changes in a sandbox do not affect production.

Build an AI-powered code review bot that reads changes from your git repository, analyzes them for security vulnerabilities, code smells, and style issues, then posts general and line-specific review comments to GitHub
An intelligent interview coordinator that automatically schedules interviews, sends confirmation emails to candidates, notifies your interview panel, and handles all follow-up communications.

Build an AI-powered Slack standup bot that posts daily standup prompts to your team channel, collects responses in organized threads, analyzes progress and blockers, and posts executive summaries to leadership channels
Users enter a portal to connect approved integrations, discover shared skills, and copy a standard MCP URL for their AI client.
copy a standard MCP URL for their AI client
Instead of sharing broad credentials or over-scoped service accounts, each user connects their own apps and keeps the permissions they should have.

Use Magic Skills for work that should be repeatable, shareable, and governed: support triage playbooks, engineering review workflows, customer handoff steps, research and reporting tasks, internal operations checklists
Let your team connect AI agents and MCP clients like Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude to approved apps, tools, and shared skills, with access controls and activity logs.
A Magic MCP server gives you a hosted MCP endpoint for a provider. Metorial manages the server and makes the provider's tools available through one connection.
The Agents area shows which agent clients have connected to Workforce and what they have done. Use it to investigate a tool call, review a session, or check how an agent connected.

Workforce is where admins turn user-authorized tool access into something AI agents and applications can use. It brings together portals, integrations, skills, Magic MCP, accounts, agents, and activity
1200+ integrations across SaaS tools, enterprise systems, data sources, and custom MCP servers.
User evaluating Composio vs Metorial noted: 'you have more robustness features to me as a developer and you're fully open source (not just the client) whereas Composio has more integrations.'

Feedback that Metorial's README lacks clarity on auth: 'I think a nod to how auth is handled would be well worth adding to the README... knowing how a consumer of MCP interacts with auth... would be very welcome.'
User reaction to launch: 'Oh my lord, your timing is perfect. I need this so badly right now... thank you for making your MCP containers available separately!'

Commenter suggested the 'Vercel for MCP' positioning was ambiguous, noting the distinction between 'Vercel for MCP [integrations]' vs '[servers]' and proposing 'Zapier for MCP' as a more fitting comparison.
